comment: The which-way world, the experiment of the heart (the owner's word of 2026-10-03, 01:52 UTC, experiments that test that it works in the engine; the advisor's matrix, #1563 comment 5964151108, T2): the two slits of examples/events/two_slits with a declared region at one gap backed by a face. Behind the lower gap a channel of the gap's rows and one more on either side runs from the wall to the screen's column between two inner faces across y (the channel's walls, from the wall's far side to the column before the screen, so that the screen's column holds no face Node and its regions keep their four rows; the Port between the channel's last Node and the screen's is a Port between two regions of the declared NodeDetector and counts for neither), and the whole channel is one declared detector, `which_way`, whose far end is the screen's column before the receding face, so that everything that passes the lower gap leaves the declared board through the channel and is credited there, and nothing of it reaches the rest of the screen; the rest of the screen is read in regions of four rows as the two slits' screen is, the channel's rows left to the channel. Three worlds from one design, laid and run alike: `which_way.json` (both gaps open, the channel), `one_gap.json` (the lower gap closed, the channel's walls standing, the same mirror for the upper gap's light) and `two_gaps.json` (both gaps open, no channel: the two slits as shipped). The blind is written by build_world.py from this design before any lay and never touched after: (1) the screen's regions behind the channel's lower wall see nothing, 0 clicks exactly (shadowed by two faces); (2) the channel's clicks are the lower gap's quanta, half the two gaps' blind total (the gaps equal and the packet symmetric about the wall's centre), and the screen's clicks in the which-way world are down by them; (3) the decisive comparison, which no Huygens row is needed for: the which-way world's screen row equals the one-gap world's screen row within the draw's scatter (the screen cannot tell the lower gap open and read from the lower gap closed: the two-slit interference term is gone exactly when the way is known), and both differ from the two-gaps world's row at the two slits' minima and maxima (the regions 4, 6 and 8); (4) a Huygens row per world as a secondary blind, the point-source sum e^(ikr) / sqrt(r) over the gaps' Nodes with the upper wall of the channel a mirror of the upper gap (Dirichlet, the face reads 0, the image source with the opposite sign) and the board's edges ignored, scaled so that the two gaps' total is the advisor's 273, a crude row (it misses the two slits' regions by up to ten at the edges, where the board's open faces reflect) printed for the shape of the pattern and no fence; one quantum one click per record throughout (the clicks never exceed the count), the draw the NodeDetectors' with the seed; fence: clicks. The screen's regions two columns deep (`screen_depth` 2, the columns 43 and 44, the channel's walls' Nodes in the column 43 left out, nothing standing on a face Node) and the draw's window one interval (`draw.window` 1), 2026-10-20, under the click's read of the board: one digit per Node read and two draws per credited quantum, so one close holds about 25 quanta per 64 Nodes; the two gaps' arrival reaches 20 quanta in one interval against the digits of 48 Nodes (refused at the interval 68 at every window), so the column before the screen is read too, carrying no inflow and drawing no click, and the window is one interval, the smallest, which held the one-gap and the which-way worlds alone at the depth 1 (their screens of 140 Nodes); every close floors its quanta once, so the quanta read stand under the blind's by about a sixth, the three worlds' readings dated in blind_and_reading.md.
